messages:
karen: Hey team — our prod app saw a bunch of user reports that the SSE stream from the Redwood API is closing with partial outputs. Happens around 10–20s after start, client receives a couple chunks then the connection ends. We have a ticket: https://zendesk.example/ticket/4521 and request-id 4f7a2b9c. Any ideas?

maria: Sorry you hit this, karen. Can you paste reproduction steps and the exact request headers? Do you see any 4xx/5xx in the client logs or just the connection close?

karen: Repro steps: open EventSource in browser or curl -N. Node code snippet:

```js
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-v2', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer <token>' } });
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('msg', e.data);
es.onerror = () => console.log('closed');
```

Curl I used:

```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-v2&prompt=hello"
```

Client log shows: "event stream closed, reconnecting" then on reconnect sometimes we get duplicate partial content. No 500 on client. Attached snippet of SSE text chunk: `data: {"delta":"Hello wo"}\n\ndata: {"delta":"rld"}\n\n` and then nothing, connection closed.

maria: Thanks — can you share the full request-id header for a failing attempt? If you have a pcap or tcpdump that'd be super helpful. Also what region (us-west/us-east/eu)?

karen: Request-id 4f7a2b9c, region us-west1. I can upload a pcap to the ticket but it's fairly large.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2121 for SSE disconnect spike (auto-detected by metrics).

dmitri: @maria ping — I'll look at runtime logs for 4f7a2b9c. Quick checks: sse connection timeouts, nginx/proxy_read settings, and whether the LB is closing TLS for idle streams. Also check streaming_disconnects and stream_chunk_flush metrics.

alex: FYI I see a small spike in streaming_disconnects around the time karen reported. Grafana panel: https://grafana.example/d/streams/streaming-metrics?from=now-1h&to=now — p95 read latency also jumps from 120ms to ~420ms for a subset of requests. Could be upstream backpressure.

maria: Suggest we ask customer to reproduce with `curl -v` so we get TLS close notifications, and capture the raw SSE frames with `curl -N --no-buffer`. Commands to run: 

```
# interactive reproduction with verbose output
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-v2&prompt=test" 2>&1 | tee curl-sse.log

# tcpdump (linux)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 port 443 -w sse_capture.pcap
```
Please redact token before upload. Also include the exact timestamp of the run.

karen: Ran curl -v and attached the logs in the ticket. Verbose shows `* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.ai left intact` immediately after the last chunk. No explicit 500. Timestamp: 2025-11-04T18:21:13Z.

dmitri: I grepped runtime logs for 4f7a2b9c — here's relevant server-side trace (redacted):

```
[2025-11-04T18:21:12Z] INFO stream-start req=4f7a2b9c model=redwood-v2 client_ip=1.2.3.4
[2025-11-04T18:21:22Z] WARN stream-flush-failed req=4f7a2b9c cause=write_timeout peer=10.0.3.12
[2025-11-04T18:21:22Z] INFO connection-closed req=4f7a2b9c code=0 reason="peer reset"
```

That `write_timeout` at the runtime layer looks suspicious — runtime tried to flush a partial frame but the socket closed. I'm going to check the ALB/NLB logs for connection resets.

alex: NLB logs show a bunch of TCP_FIN or RSTs around 18:21:22 from idle connections older than 15s. Our load balancer has an idle timeout of 15s for TLS connections in this region. That matches the 10–20s window customers see.

maria: Good find. So the LB is likely closing TLS before the runtime can finish sending the last buffered chunk. That would cause write_timeouts and client sees an abrupt close with partial content. Workarounds: 1) increase LB idle timeout; 2) ensure runtime sends keepalive comments/events periodically; 3) enable streaming chunk flush more frequently.

karen: Can you suggest a quick fix we can apply in our client while you fix infra? We still need production users.

dmitri: Client-side options: add a short keepalive ping (comment frame) from server is best. For client-only workaround — implement de-dup on reconnection (keep last token position) and allow a short backoff before reconnect to avoid duplicate partial pieces. Also set EventSource retry to a higher value so LB isn't seeing many rapid connects (which can exacerbate state).

maria: I'm going to open an infra task to increase the NLB idle timeout in us-west1 to 120s and also push a runtime change: emit SSE comment `: keepalive\n\n` every 10s for long-running streams. dmitri — can you prepare the runtime patch?

dmitri: On it. Patch will add periodic flush of comment frames and a config flag `sse_keepalive_interval_ms`. I'll also add metric `sse_keepalive_sent`. Proposed default 10000ms.

alex: I'll update infra to roll NLB timeout and monitor streaming_disconnects. I'll add a Grafana alert if stream_disconnect_rate > 0.5% for 5m after the change.

karen: Thanks. After your change we did a smoke test and streams stayed alive for 2+ minutes and no partial outputs. Customer confirmed reduced tickets.

maria: Resolution notes: root cause = NLB idle timeout closing TLS before runtime flushed final SSE chunk. Fixes: increased NLB idle timeout (us-west1) and runtime change to send SSE keepalive comments every 10s. Added de-dup guidance for clients and created INC-2121 for follow-up (monitoring and backfill config).

ops-bot: INC-2121 updated: status=resolved, linked PR=https://git.example/redwood/runtime/pulls/897

karen: Great — thanks all :tada:
